As the new school year begins, more and more Americans are expressing support for an outright ban on student phone use during class.

With the new school year underway, support for banning iPhones in classrooms continues to rise.

Yes, it's still July, but summer is somehow already over for some reason. My own kids go back to school today and tomorrow — marking the second year in a row that the first day of school falls outside of August.

Apple is rolling out its annual "Back to School" promotion to match the season, offering eligible students and educators a gift card of up to $150 when they purchase select Mac and iPad models before August 27. Consumers in several states can also take advantage of limited-time sales tax holidays.

While back-to-school discounts are a pleasant perk, smartphone use during class hours is increasingly falling out of favor.

The most upvoted comment comes from GreenPizza.

I have not seen any data supporting the claim that student phone use reduces the risk of school shootings. The reality is that reducing classroom distractions is what truly gets us back to the original purpose of going to school — learning.

A new survey from the Pew Research Center found that 77% of American adults support banning middle school students from using phones in class. That figure is up from 68% in 2024 and 74% in 2025, with just 18% now opposing classroom bans.

Support for stricter, all-day "bell-to-bell" bans is growing even faster. The share of Americans who support prohibiting students from using phones during school hours has, for the first time, surpassed those who oppose it.

The report also noted that younger adults remain less enthusiastic about both classroom bans and all-day bans, but support has risen across all age groups since 2024. You can read the full report here.

What do you think? Should schools restrict iPhone use to class time only, implement a full "bell-to-bell" ban, or leave the decision to students and parents? Let us know in the comments.
